title: Rapid-Acting Mental Health Treatment Returns on May 16, 2026!
subtitle: RAMHT, the live-action newsletter event, returns to San Francisco next month.
body_html:
For my readers, in moments unamused, it can be tempting to despair. “If only this amusing and informative newsletter could be a live event!” I imagine them weeping, quietly, as they lay their heads down to sleep. Dear readers, your cries of pain have been heard, no matter how quiet! And, forsooth, an event exists to provide sweet succor for your woe.

It’s a Grady Hannah and The Frontier Psychiatrists production!

On May 16, 2026, on the first night of the American Psychiatric Association Annual Meeting, we return to San Francisco to have rapid conversations about rapid-acting treatments and assessments.

First, A Brain Medicine News Roundup!

  • Robert Glatter, M.D., and your own Dr. Muir wrote a nice article this week, published on Healio. It’s about the new indication of TMS treatment in adolescent depression.

Meta-analyses through March 2025 demonstrate significant efficacy, with high-frequency repetitive or rTMS showing the largest treatment effects. While FDA clearance has been extended to patients as young as 15 years, real-world data from 1,257 patients aged 11 to 21 years show promising safety and efficacy profiles, supporting insurance coverage expansion like Highmark's decision to cover TMS down to patients aged 11 years.

  • Blue Shield California is covering SAINT neuromodulation for depression! This is due, in no small part, to the efforts of Brandon Bentzley, M.D., Ph.D., of whom I’ve written before.

  • Neurolief’s ProLiv™Rx is now a covered treatment for depression in the VA system for our Veterans. It’s an at-home treatment for depression that moves beyond yet another adjunctive medication. Also, Neurolief raises another $6M in the process.

  • GH Research's GH001, an inhaled, ultra-rapid acting, 5-MeO-DMT-based therapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression (TRD), demonstrated a robust outcome in Phase 2b trials, with 57.5% of patients achieving remission by day 8, compared to 0% in the placebo group.

  • My own team member, Ava Meyer, NP, is on WFXB, talking about Brain Medicine.

  • And, in a moment of self-promotion, my book is available in print! Inessential Pharmacology is available from Amazon (affiliate link), in both hardback and paperback.

Now, back to RAMHT…(it’s pronounced Ramp-t, not Ram-it).

It’s an event with sponsors who, paradoxically, choose to drop the corporate speak and speak openly about the revolution in brain medicine as it collides with AI. Our event has also been a place where new data and big news updates are announced to the world. Remember when Ibogaine’s potential was made clear in Nature Medicine? At RAMHT #1. Beckley Clinical’s $20m fundraise? At RAMHT #5. Samnai, even existing as a company? Out of stealth at RAMHT #1. We make news—then the audience gets to mingle with those very news makers. Tell your journalist friends!

Get a ticket now—also, it’s free if you're an APA member. Just email us at ramhtevents@gmail.com for your free code.
